scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested building an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED (E-04).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Since August 2026, CRM dispute-ticket volume has roughly doubled (610→1260/month) primarily because a majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carry an ACTUAL meter read that was accepted into billing despite being erroneous, with billing import/validation currently treating ACTUAL reads as trusted and not catching this error (E-04). A smaller share of disputes stems from estimate substitution tied to a manual-read route completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01). The surge is not attributable to slow ticket response (within SLA, E-02) or a tariff change (none logged, E-05).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: Route-log still shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 — that process shortfall is real. It no longer means this shortfall explains the ESTIMATED-dispute segment: E-12 shows only 56 of 1240 (4.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills match the 'no read received' pattern consistent with missed manual reads, while 1184 (95.5%) had a valid pre-cutoff read that billing import rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) — an AMI/import mechanism, not route lateness.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Dispute-ticket response times are median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2,440 tickets.

F-03.statement: CRM dispute volume rose from 610 (2026-06) and 590 (2026-07) to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09), roughly doubling from the Jun-Jul baseline.

F-04.statement: Of disputed bills, 1785 had read_type ACTUAL and 1240 had read_type ESTIMATED (3025 total).

F-05.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records for the surge period, indicating no tariff change occurred.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle shows 320 accounts (40 distinct routes) had an estimated read in the last billing cycle.

F-08.statement: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 routes currently below completion target, each with a distinct completion rate (fields: completion, route; sample route R-00 at 0.70).

F-09.statement: Of accounts with disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 had an AMI read before cutoff on firmware v4.2 that was exported to billing but rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

F-10.statement: Of accounts with disputed ESTIMATED bills, 56 had no AMI read received before cutoff (mixed firmware) and so none was exported to billing.

F-11.statement: mdms-export.meter_firmware_units records firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) with register_unit '0.1 m3', and firmware v3.x with register_unit 'm3'.

F-12.statement: billing-config rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) checks raw register value against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling 'none'; rule BV-09 (deployed 2026-03-02) was only a label-text change.

F-13.statement: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts returned 1184 account-level records, all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (540 distinct ami_read_ts values).

F-14.statement: billing-db's own affected_accounts_v42 query returns the same 1184 accounts (firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) already identified via mdms-export, confirming the population from a second authoritative source.

F-15.statement: billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed independently returns 1184 records (firmware v4.2, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and 56 records (mixed firmware, import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED), matching E-12's breakdown from a second authoritative source.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-AUTOMATABLE.statement: The August-September dispute surge stems from inadequate ticket response capacity/speed, and both auto-answering tickets and auto-correcting bills via an AI agent will resolve it.

H-AMI-MDMS-PIPELINE-FAILURE.statement: AMI read delivery or MDMS validation began failing or degrading around August, producing bad/estimated reads that generated incorrect bills and drove the dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reading completion dropped or became unreliable around August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills, independent of ticket handling speed.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (e.g., read-type acceptance or estimate logic) around August introduced systematic bill errors that drove the dispute surge.

H-BILL-ACCURACY-UNCHANGED-PERC.statement: Bills remain as accurate as before August and the ticket surge reflects customer reaction to a rate/tariff or billing-cycle change rather than any pipeline or process defect.

H-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) carried an ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED, suggesting incorrect actual meter reads (field or AMI-sourced) being accepted into billing may be a larger driver of disputes than estimate substitution.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: The field reading contractor has been short three readers since July, causing manual-read routes to run behind schedule and forcing estimate substitution for affected accounts, driving part of the dispute surge.

H-AMI-HIGHCONSUMP-REJECT.statement: AMI reads from firmware v4.2 meters are being rejected by billing import under a high-consumption validation rule (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and driving the vast majority (1184 of 1240) of disputed ESTIMATED bills.

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH.statement: Firmware v4.2 AMI meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3 versus the m3 units of older v3.x firmware; if the import or validation path treats v4.2 values as plain m3 without converting, consumption would appear ~10x inflated, producing the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern seen in E-12 for exactly those reads.

H-BV17-NO-UNIT-CONVERSION.statement: Billing-config rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history without unit scaling; since v4.2 firmware (rolled out 2026-06) reports in 0.1 m3 units, valid high-register v4.2 reads appear ~10x over history and are rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, matching the Aug-Sep surge timing and the 1184/1240 split in E-12.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows manual-read route completion of only 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts during Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. a real shortfall in field meter-read collection coinciding with the dispute surge window. This points to a tangible process gap (missed manual reads forcing estimate substitution) rather than merely a ticket-handling or tariff-perception issue.

Route-log still shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 — that process shortfall is real. It no longer means this shortfall explains the ESTIMATED-dispute segment: E-12 shows only 56 of 1240 (4.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills match the 'no read received' pattern consistent with missed manual reads, while 1184 (95.5%) had a valid pre-cutoff read that billing import rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) — an AMI/import mechanism, not route lateness.

CRM data shows dispute-ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA across 2,440 tickets, so ticket-handling speed is not a bottleneck in the current surge; the problem is not that staff respond too slowly.

CRM dispute-volume data shows roughly a doubling of monthly disputes (≈600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 to ≈1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026), confirming the magnitude and timing of the surge described in the initial request, but it carries no information about the underlying cause.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED read type (3025 total), i.e. the majority of disputed bills carried an ACTUAL read, not an ESTIMATED one — estimate substitution accounts for only ~41% of disputed bills.

Billing-db still shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED (3025 total) — that count and split are unchanged and valid. It no longer means the ESTIMATED minority is attributable to a route-completion/estimate-substitution process gap as the root problem framed it: E-12 shows 1184 of those 1240 (95.5%) stem from AMI high-consumption rejection of valid reads, so the premise's claimed mechanism for the 'smaller share' is wrong for nearly all of it, and the majority ACTUAL-read clause of the premise remains unaddressed by this new evidence.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged around the dispute surge; this rules out a tariff change as the driver and specifically undercuts the tariff-change clause of H-BILL-ACCURACY-UNCHANGED-PERC.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that there has been no tariff change this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-05) that no tariff change occurred during the surge; it adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating that record.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims the field reading team has been short three readers since July, causing manual-read routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills instead. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder explanation for the route completion shortfall, not independently verified, and comes from a stakeholder with a stated incentive toward headcount increase and a bias toward attributing problems to staffing.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) confirms that while the utility may request route priority changes, execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager — this is the authoritative basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update and for success criterion SC-NO-UNCONFIRMED-DISPATCH-CHAN. It does not speak to the cause of the dispute surge.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returns 14 distinct routes each with its own completion rate (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 88% manual-read completion shortfall; it contains no cause (staffing or otherwise) for the lateness.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI, a non-authoritative stakeholder source, reports via vendor ticket TX-4471 that MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned, which, if accurate, would remove the access blocker that previously left mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated ACCESS_PENDING and made DA-MDMS investigation infeasible in contest time. The claim is unverified against the authoritative tool itself (mdms-export tool_health is still recorded DEGRADED) and comes from the vendor-side engineer, not an independent confirmation.

mdms-export's read_events_for_disputed_estimated query shows that of accounts with disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 had a valid AMI read before cutoff (firmware v4.2) that billing import rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION despite it being exported, while only 56 had no AMI read received at all; these two counts sum to 1240, exactly matching E-04's total ESTIMATED-read dispute count. This indicates the ESTIMATED-dispute segment is driven almost entirely by an AMI/billing-import rejection of high-consumption reads, not by manual field-read lateness.

E-13 shows mdms-export's meter firmware catalog has two generations: firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) with register_unit "0.1 m3", versus older firmware v3.x with register_unit "m3" — a 10x scale difference. The June 2026 rollout timing precedes the August surge, giving a concrete, testable mechanism (unit-scale mismatch) that could explain why valid v4.2 AMI reads are flagged REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION in E-12, without yet showing which stage (MDMS conversion or billing-import validation) fails to account for it.

E-14.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config shows rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, exactly at the surge onset) checks raw register value against 12-month m3 consumption history with "unit_scaling":"none"; the other logged change, BV-09, was only a label-text edit (2026-03-02) and is irrelevant. Combined with E-13's firmware v4.2 register units of 0.1 m3, this pinpoints a concrete, testable mechanism for the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern in E-12: unconverted raw v4.2 register values appearing ~10x over history.

U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.question: Is the mechanism producing erroneous ACTUAL meter reads an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure, a billing import validation rule change, or field meter-reading error?
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must target the AMI vendor pipeline, a billing-config rule rollback, or field reading QA, and whether any fix requires a protected write under K-BILLWRITE.
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.resolution_path: Obtain the vendor-provisioned MDMS AMI read event export (currently ACCESS_PENDING per recovery log) and review the billing-config rule change log for the August 2026 period.
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.safe_placeholder: Continue manual review/flagging of disputed ACTUAL-read accounts; do not deploy any automated billing fix until the root mechanism is confirmed.
U-ROOT-MECHANISM-UNRESOLVED.resolution: E-14 shows the rejection mechanism traces to a billing-config validation rule (BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01) lacking unit scaling, not an AMI/MDMS delivery or validation pipeline failure; combined with E-13 (v4.2 register units of 0.1 m3) this points to a billing-import rule defect, pending confirmation that correcting it eliminates the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.question: How much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority is actually explained by the field staffing shortage SH-FIELD describes, versus other causes?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.decision_impact: Affects whether any dispatch or staffing remediation is warranted and in what proportion relative to the ACTUAL-read mechanism.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion/staffing trends against the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputed bills.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.safe_placeholder: Treat SH-FIELD's staffing explanation as unverified; take no dispatch or headcount action on it alone.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-UNVERI.resolution: E-12 shows the full ESTIMATED-read dispute minority (1240 accounts, matching E-04) is explained by AMI-side causes: 1184 by a billing-import high-consumption rejection and 56 by no AMI read received, leaving no evident contribution from field staffing/route lateness to this AMI-metered segment.

U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.question: Does aggregate monthly dispute volume alone validly measure resolution, given disputes split across a confirmed BV-17/unit-mismatch cause and an unestablished ACTUAL-read cause with likely different fixes and timelines?
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.decision_impact: Determines whether SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE should be judged on the aggregate trend alone or require cause-decomposed tracking.
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.resolution_path: Decompose M-DISPUTE-VOLUME-TREND by dispute cause (BV-17 unit mismatch vs ACTUAL-read vs other) before declaring the baseline criterion met.
U-METRIC-DECOMPOSITION-VALIDIT.safe_placeholder: Report decomposed cause-level metrics alongside the aggregate trend rather than relying on the aggregate alone to judge success.

U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.question: What mechanism explains the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) that carry an ACTUAL read type, given the BV-17/unit-mismatch mechanism explains only the ESTIMATED-dispute segment?
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether any future bill-correction scope should extend beyond the confirmed unit-mismatch ESTIMATED segment to the larger ACTUAL-read segment.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-db for disputed ACTUAL-read accounts' meter/firmware/account attributes and correlate against known defect patterns (firmware generation, rule exposure) similar to the E-12 ESTIMATED-segment analysis.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Limit any proposed bill-correction scope to the confirmed unit-mismatch ESTIMATED segment (1184 accounts, E-12) and exclude ACTUAL-read disputes until this mechanism is established.

A-UPSTREAM-READ-DEFECT-SOURCE.statement: The erroneous ACTUAL reads are assumed to originate from an upstream read/validation defect (field reading, AMI telemetry, or MDMS validation) rather than a billing calculation error, though the exact source among AMI/MDMS pipeline failure or a billing rule change is not yet confirmed.

A-FIELD-STAFFING-MINORITY-CONT.statement: Field staffing shortage (SH-FIELD's claim) is assumed to be a plausible but unverified contributor to the smaller ESTIMATED-read portion of disputes, since it comes from a non-authoritative, potentially biased source.

A-RULE-LOG-COMPLETE.statement: The billing-config validation_rule_changes log (completeness UNKNOWN) is assumed to capture all relevant rule changes in the surge window, i.e. BV-17 and BV-09 are the only changes affecting the ESTIMATED-dispute mechanism.

A-FIRMWARE-BATCH-SCOPE.statement: The 0.1 m3 vs m3 register-unit distinction is assumed to apply uniformly across all firmware v4.2 meters, with no mixed/partial rollout complicating the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern.

A-BV17-FIX-SUFFICIENT.statement: Correcting BV-17 to apply unit scaling for v4.2 reads is assumed sufficient to eliminate future REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION estimate substitutions for those meters, with no other downstream step also mishandling the unit mismatch.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute-ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03).
Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 (95.5%) had a valid pre-cutoff AMI read rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rather than a missed read (E-12).
1785 of 3025 disputed bills carry an ACTUAL read type, a majority segment whose dispute mechanism is not yet explained (E-04).
Dispute ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d vs 3.0d SLA, 2,440 tickets), ruling out slow response as the driver (E-02).
problem_definition.root_problem: Since August 2026, CRM dispute-ticket volume roughly doubled (610→1260/month, E-03). The dominant confirmed mechanism: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none' (E-14), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); valid v4.2 reads therefore appear ~10x inflated and are rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (95.5%, E-12). This is a billing-config defect, not an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure (H-AMI-MDMS-PIPELINE-FAILURE rejected by E-14) nor field staffing/route lateness (rejected by E-12). The mechanism behind the separate majority of disputed bills carrying an ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-04) remains unestablished by current evidence.

proposal.root_problem: Since August 2026, CRM dispute-ticket volume roughly doubled (610→1260/month, E-03). The dominant confirmed mechanism: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none' (E-14), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); valid v4.2 reads therefore appear ~10x inflated and are rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution that accounts for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (95.5%, E-12). This is a billing-config defect, not an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure (H-AMI-MDMS-PIPELINE-FAILURE rejected by E-14) nor field staffing/route lateness (rejected by E-12). The mechanism behind the separate majority of disputed bills carrying an ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-04) remains unestablished by current evidence.

symptoms: CRM dispute-ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03).

proposal.affected_process: P-M2C meter-to-cash: billing import validation stage
causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 AMI meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3, versus m3 for older v3.x firmware (E-13).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling 'none', not converting v4.2's 0.1 m3 readings (E-14).
Valid v4.2 AMI reads therefore appear roughly 10x over historical consumption and billing import rejects them with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12, E-14).
Rejected reads are excluded from billing, so those accounts receive an ESTIMATED bill instead of the valid actual reading, accounting for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (95.5%) (E-12).
Customers who received an estimated bill despite a valid, legitimate high actual reading file dispute tickets, contributing to the Aug-Sep CRM dispute-volume surge (E-03, E-12).

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and 'fix whatever is causing the wrong bills' after dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1260/month since August (CL-01, E-03). Investigation first framed the problem as mostly bad ACTUAL reads plus a smaller route-lateness-driven ESTIMATED segment (PD-1@v1), but that framing was invalidated when E-12 showed 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (95.5%) actually came from AMI reads that billing rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not from missed field reads. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) pins this down to a confirmed billing-config defect: rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-14), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13), making valid readings look ~10x inflated and get rejected -- confirmed from two independent authoritative sources (E-12/E-15 via mdms-export, E-16/E-17 via billing-db). Field staffing shortage and AMI/MDMS pipeline failure were tested and rejected as causes of this segment (contradicted by E-12/E-17 and E-14 respectively). The release decision is HOLD: a Layer-1 safety/verification check failed because 6 required actual_read_dispute_accounts_raw records are missing, and the underlying mechanism for the separate, larger ACTUAL-read dispute segment (1785 of 3025 bills, E-04) was never established. No bill writes or dispatch changes were made or proposed; the only release-scope deliverable was the confirmed BV-17 unit-mismatch diagnosis, and even that could not clear the safety predicate needed to proceed to release.
key_points: The surge is confirmed real: CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03), and is not explained by slow ticket response (within SLA, E-02) or a tariff change (none logged, E-05/E-06).

Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 (95.5%) trace to a confirmed billing-config defect: rule BV-17 lacks unit scaling (E-14) while firmware v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 (E-13), causing valid reads to be misclassified REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12), independently corroborated by E-15, E-16, and E-17.

Field staffing shortage (SH-FIELD's claim, E-07) and an AMI/MDMS pipeline failure were investigated and rejected as causes of the ESTIMATED-dispute surge, since the dominant mechanism is a billing-import rule issue, not a read-collection or telemetry failure (contradicted by E-12, E-14, E-17).

The majority of disputed bills carry an ACTUAL read type (1785 of 3025, E-04), and the mechanism behind that larger segment remains unestablished; it is tracked as unknown U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM and open verification obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM, explicitly outside this release's scope.
